It runs in Node.js, browsers, and bundler-based environments (React, Angular, Vite, Webpack, Electron), and requires no PowerPoint installation or license. Output is standards-compliant Open Office XML (OOXML), compatible with Microsoft PowerPoint, Apple Keynote, LibreOffice Impress, and Google Slides (via import).\n\n## About this fork\n\nThis repository is a fork of [gitbrent/PptxGenJS](https://github.com/gitbrent/PptxGenJS), maintained for the PPTist / ScioBot stack and published as `@lofcz/pptxgenjs`. It tracks hardening work from [NEOMA GmbH](https://neo-ma.de)'s distribution (`@neo-ma/pptxgenjs`):\n\n- **Strict null-safety** — the entire source compiles under TypeScript `strictNullChecks` with zero non-null assertions (`!`) and zero unchecked `as` casts; null-safety is enforced through explicit types, guard clauses, and validated defaults\n- **Continuous integration** — unit, end-to-end, and golden-file OOXML snapshot tests run on Node.js 20 and 22\n- **Security** — no known vulnerabilities in the published package, and a published [security policy](SECURITY.md)\n\nThe public API remains compatible with upstream PptxGenJS; existing code and documentation continue to apply.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Node.js 20 or newer\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\nnpm install @lofcz/pptxgenjs\n```\n\n```bash\nyarn add @lofcz/pptxgenjs\n```\n\nThe package ships dual ES Module and CommonJS builds. Bundlers select the correct build automatically via the `exports` field in `package.json`. The `.pptx` output can be delivered as a browser download, base64 string, Blob, Buffer, or Node stream.\n\n## Quick start\n\nA presentation is created in four steps: instantiate, add a slide, add content, save.\n\n```typescript\nimport pptxgen from \"@lofcz/pptxgenjs\";\n\n// 1. Create a presentation\nconst pres = new pptxgen();\n\n// 2. Add a slide\nconst slide = pres.addSlide();\n\n// 3. Add content (text, tables, shapes, images, charts, media)\nslide.addText(\"Quarterly Results\", { x: 0.5, y: 0.5, fontSize: 24, bold: true });\nslide.addText(\"Revenue up 12% year over year\", { x: 0.5, y: 1.3, fontSize: 14, color: \"363636\" });\n\n// 4. Write the .pptx file\nawait pres.writeFile({ fileName: \"quarterly-results.pptx\" });\n```\n\nWhen loading the library via a `<script>` tag rather than a module import, the constructor is the global `PptxGenJS` (for example, `const pres = new PptxGenJS()`); the remaining steps are identical.\n\n## Documentation\n\nComplete API reference, tutorials, and integration guides are available on the official docs site: [https://gitbrent.github.io/PptxGenJS](https://gitbrent.github.io/PptxGenJS).\n\nLocal VitePress docs under [`docs/`](docs) can be previewed with `npm run docs:dev`.\n\n## Issues and support\n\nReport defects and feature requests on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/lofcz/PptxGenJS/issues/new), or [submit a pull request](https://github.com/lofcz/PptxGenJS/pulls). === assistant ===
**Verified with E2E — root cause found and fixed.**

`html-to-image` only paints MathLive/KaTeX when the node is **fully opaque and in the viewport**. The old `left:-99999px` mount produced blank white PNGs (`ink=0`), so export fell back to raw LaTeX.

| Strategy | Ink pixels | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `left:-99999px` (old) | 0 | blank white |
| `opacity:0.01` | 0 | blank |
| **viewport + opacity:1 + cover** | **11450** | **rendered math** |

**Fix in** `PPTist/src/hooks/useExport.ts`: mount at `(0,0)` with `opacity:1`, put a white cover on top (no flash), then `toPng`.

**Proof:** `node scripts/e2e-math-export/run.mjs` → `PASS: production-path has visible math ink` (ink=11450). Saved PNG shows real fractions (`v = s/t`, etc.), not LaTeX source.

Re-export the deck from a PPTist build that includes this change — math should appear as images in PowerPoint, not `\frac{...}` text.

=== assistant ===
That red CORS line is from **PPTist still probing the image with a browser `fetch` before using your proxy**.

`sciencefacts.net` allows `<img>` display but blocks CORS reads. Export then does:

1. `fetch('https://www.sciencefacts.net/...')` → **fails** (browser always logs this, even if caught)
2. `exportMediaResolver` → `media-fetch` edge → works

So the proxy was already wired in sciobot; the console error was left over from step 1. It’s noise, not “CORS is broken again.”

**Fix (in local PPTist):** for cross-origin URLs, go straight to `exportMediaResolver` and **never** do the doomed direct fetch.

Until you publish a new `@lofcz/pptist` and bump sciobot past `2.0.29`, production will keep logging that line on every export that hits third-party images.

=== assistant ===
{"type":"tool_use","name":"CallMcpTool","input":{"server":"user-context7","toolName":"query-docs","arguments":{"libraryId":"/gitbrent/pptxgenjs","query":"Does PptxGenJS support math equations, OMML, LaTeX, or formula objects in slides?"}}}


=== assistant ===
Because **nothing in the export stack can emit PowerPoint math**.

PowerPoint’s editable equations are **OMML** (`m:oMath` in the slide XML). What we have today:

| Layer | What it supports |
|---|---|
| **PPTist** | Math as MathLive/LaTeX in HTML (`span.pptist-math` + `data-latex`) |
| **PptxGenJS** | Text runs (`a:t`), images, shapes — **no equations API** |
| **Export** | Rasterize the box (or SVG for `latex` elements) so it *looks* right |

So export has three bad options:

1. **Image** (current) — looks correct, not editable  
2. **Raw LaTeX / plain text** — editable, looks wrong (`\frac`, missing subscripts)  
3. **Real OMML** — not implemented; would need LaTeX→OMML + PptxGenJS support to write `m:oMath`

The `mathPlus` / `mathDivide` stuff in PptxGenJS is just **shape icon names**, not formulas.

**Bottom line:** images aren’t a preference — they’re the only path that preserves layout until someone builds OMML export. That’s a real feature (converter + library work), not a small tweak.

If you want to pursue it, the next step is LaTeX→OMML in PptxGenJS and wiring PPTist to emit those instead of PNGs.

=== assistant ===
Yes. Mixed text + math is the primary path.

`formatHTML` walks the HTML AST and emits **interleaved runs** in one text box:

- plain text → `{ text: 'Konstantní rychlost: ' }`
- `span.pptist-math` → `{ text: '', options: { omml } }`
- more plain text after → another text run

PptxGenJS puts those in the same `<a:p>`: `<a:r>…text…</a:r>` next to `<m:oMath>…</m:oMath>`. That’s covered by the OMML test (`Speed: ` + fraction) and the export E2E (`Konstantní rychlost: ` + `v=s/t`).

So a line like `Ft = f · Fn` with only the formula marked as math exports as editable equation inline with the surrounding words — not as a full-box image.

**ECMA-376 §5.1.5.2.6 `p` (Text Paragraphs), `CT_TextParagraph`** (merged PDF, page 3394):

```xml
<complexType name="CT_TextParagraph">
 <sequence>
 <element name="pPr" type="CT_TextParagraphProperties" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1"/>
 <group ref="EG_TextRun" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded"/>
 <element name="endParaRPr" type="CT_TextCharacterProperties" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1"/>
 </sequence>
</complexType>
```

**§7.1.2.77 `oMath` / §7.1.2.78 `oMathPara`** (page 5049–5051): `oMath` is the equation element; its content model is `EG_OMathElements` (runs, `f`, `rad`, `sSup`, …). PowerPoint places `m:oMath` as a child of the paragraph — which our pipeline already did correctly.

**The violation:** `pPr` has `maxOccurs="1"` and must be the *first* child of `a:p`. The user's broken `slide3.xml` showed exactly the violation — one paragraph with **two** `<a:pPr>` blocks (bullet props before the text run, then `buNone` props again before the `<m:oMath>`):

```xml
<a:p><a:pPr marL="251460" ...><a:buChar char="•"/></a:pPr><a:r>...Konstantní rychlost...</a:r><a:pPr indent="0" marL="0">...<a:buNone/></a:pPr><m:oMath>...</m:oMath>...</a:p>
```

Text-only files survived because PowerPoint is lenient there; once `m:oMath` is present, the repair drops everything after the schema violation — hence "repairable, missing elements".

I've already fixed this in `gen-xml.ts`: `genXmlTextBody` now emits **one** `a:pPr` per paragraph (derived from the first run, placed first), matching `CT_TextParagraph`. All 69 PptxGenJS tests pass, and the snapshot diff confirms the duplicate `pPr` is gone. Now let me build, bump, and verify end-to-end with the PPTist harness.

=== assistant ===
I've now actually read the relevant spec pages from both PDFs, and they confirm the root cause. Here's what the standards say and what I fixed:

## What the specs say (verified by extracting the actual pages)

**`pptx_standard.pdf` ([MS-PPTX] v20240820)** — §2.2.8 "Math Extensions" is only about the `a14:m` shape-autofit extension; embedding itself is defined in ECMA-376.

**`ECMA-376-new-merged.pdf`** — the decisive passages:

- **§5.1.5.2.6 `p` (Text Paragraphs), `CT_TextParagraph`** (page 4182): the content model is a strict sequence — `pPr` with **`minOccurs=0 maxOccurs=1`**, then `EG_TextRun` (runs) unbounded, then `endParaRPr`. So **at most one `a:pPr`, and it must be the first child of `a:p`**. That is exactly what our exporter violated — the old code emitted a fresh `a:pPr` before *every* run, which your invalid file confirms (e.g. two `pPr` blocks in the "Konstantní rychlost" paragraph).
- **§7.1 Math / §7.1.2.77–78 `oMath`/`oMathPara`** (pages 5749, 5837–5839): `oMath` wraps a single equation of runs (`m:r`/`m:t`) and functions (`m:f` with `m:num`/`m:den`, etc.) — matching what we emit via `mathml2omml`.

PowerPoint tolerates duplicate `pPr` in text-only slides but repairs **destructively** once `m:oMath` appears — that's your "repairable file with missing elements."

## The fix

`PptxGenJS/src/gen-xml.ts` (`genXmlTextBody`): paragraph properties are now emitted **exactly once**, derived from the first run, as the first child of `a:p`; the per-run `pPr` emission is removed. Added a regression test (`Schema: a paragraph contains at most one a:pPr`) asserting every generated paragraph has ≤1 `pPr`, placed first — plus the full suite still passes (69/69, snapshots updated to the corrected single-`pPr` output).

Verified end-to-end in PPTist (`npm run test:omml-export`, now with an extra `pPrViolations` check):

```
pPrViolations: []   oMathCount: 3   mixedInSameParagraph: true   mediaCount: 0
PASS: PPTX contains native OMML math (mixed text+math, no media images)
```

Selectively ported from `yukosgiti:feature/custom-data-labels` — not a blind cherry-pick.

### Kept
- **`dataLabels?: string[]`** on public `OptsChartData` (bar/line/area + pie)
- **Rich-text `c:dLbl` / `c:tx` / `c:rich`** emission
- **XML escaping** (`encodeXmlEntities`) — their sanitize fix

### Skipped
- `jszip` downgrade
- `dist/` / `demos/` rebuild artifacts
- Merge / revert / whitespace-only commits
- Their types rewrite that narrowed `labels` to `string[][]` only

### Fixed vs upstream
| Their code | Ours |
|---|---|
| Hardcoded `dLblPos="ctr"` | Honors `dataLabelPosition` |
| Hardcoded `showVal="1"` | `showVal="0"` (custom text replaces value, same as scatter) |
| `opts.fontSize` | `dataLabelFontSize` + color/face/bold/italic |
| Only on internal `IOptsChartData` | On public `OptsChartData` + `types` |
| Drops series `numFmt` when any custom labels | Keeps series defaults; sparse custom labels only where defined |

slide.addChart(pptx.ChartType.bar, [{

=== assistant ===
Integrated [liyao1520/pptx-embed-fonts](https://github.com/liyao1520/pptx-embed-fonts) into `@lofcz/pptxgenjs`.

**What landed**
- Dependency: `pptx-embed-fonts@^0.0.6`
- `pptx.addFont({ fontFace, fontFile, fontType })` API
- Embeds into the zip **before** `generateAsync` (no double pack)
- Dynamic import — font stack loads only when fonts were registered
- Types + regression test (IBM Plex Sans fixture)

**Usage**
```ts
const fontFile = await fetch('/fonts/MyFont.ttf').then(r => r.arrayBuffer())
await pptx.addFont({ fontFace: 'MyFont', fontFile, fontType: 'ttf' })
slide.addText('Hello', { fontFace: 'MyFont', fontSize: 24 })
await pptx.writeFile({ fileName: 'out.pptx' })
```

Supported types: `ttf` | `otf` | `woff` | `eot`.

PPTist export is not wired yet — say if you want `useExport` to call `addFont` for loaded custom fonts.

### Fixes vs upstream
1. **Exactly 12 colors** — short arrays no longer produce `val="undefined"`; invalid length falls back to Office defaults with a warning  
2. **Hue units** — `hue` / `hueOff` use deg × 60000; `hueMod` stays percent × 1000 (upstream used ×1000 for all)  
3. **No double-apply** — modifiers applied once in `createColorElement`; bare `ModifiedThemeColor` is not treated as `ShapeFillProps`  
4. **Gradients/patterns preserved** — `isModifiedThemeColor` guard before fill-type handling  
5. **`lumMod` etc. not clamped** — values > 100 stay valid (Office themes use 110%)

### Touched
`core-interfaces.ts`, `gen-utils.ts`, `gen-xml.ts` (`makeXmlTheme`), `gen-charts.ts` (dPt + gridlines via `createColorElement`), `types/index.d.ts`, tests

=== assistant ===
Selective port of **sambauers/gradients** is in — kept our nested `type:'gradient'` API and added their flat API on top.

### Supported (sambauers-compatible)
```ts
fill: {
  type: 'linearGradient',
  angle: 45,
  scaled: true,
  flip: 'x',
  tileRect: { t: 10, l: 0 },
  stops: [
    { position: 0, color: '000000', transparency: 10 },
    { position: 100, color: '333333', transparency: 50 },
  ],
}
```

### Also added to nested gradients
- `flip`, `tileRect`, `rotWithShape` alias, stop `position` alias for `pos`

### Fixes vs upstream
- Always emit `<a:lin>` (they skipped angle `0`)
- Still require ≥2 stops (fallback to solid)
- Kept radial + pattern fills (their rewrite dropped those)

Did **not** take their `SolidShapeFillProps` / `LinearGradientShapeFillProps` split — it would break our existing gradient/pattern API.

=== assistant ===
**Root cause:** PowerPoint silently strips bare `<m:oMath>` from slides (no error). Your kinematika file had OMML in XML, but PowerPoint dropped it on open — confirmed by COM open→save (3 equations → 0).

**Fix:** Wrap math in `<a14:m>` (DrawingML 2010), which PowerPoint keeps. After round-trip: **4/4 equations survived**, and the PNG shows stacked fractions inline with Czech text.

**Proof demo (open this):**
- `C:\Users\mstagl-dev\Downloads\pptxgenjs-inline-math-proof.pptx`
- Screenshot: `PptxGenJS\test\prove-math-out\inline-math-proof-slide.png`

Re-run anytime:
```bash
npx tsx test/prove-math-renders.mjs
```

**Library change:** `normalizeOmml` now emits `<a14:m><m:oMath>…</m:oMath></a14:m>`, slide root gets `xmlns:a14` + `mc:Ignorable="a14"`, and math shapes get `txBox="1"`.

PPTist still uses published `@lofcz/pptxgenjs@4.1.2` without this wrap — rebuild/publish the fork and bump the dependency for exports to pick it up.

You have access to MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools through `GetMcpTools` and `CallMcpTool`.

## MCP Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetMcpTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallMcpTool` to invoke them. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one `GetMcpTools` call followed by one `CallMcpTool` call.

If the user mentions, references, or links to a product or service that corresponds to an available MCP server, and the request likely depends on information from that service, proactively inspect that MCP server before answering. Do not wait for the user to explicitly ask you to use MCP. If you are unsure which server matches, use `GetMcpTools` with a pattern based on the service name.

`GetMcpTools` supports four modes:

1. `{"server":"<id>"}`: returns full input schemas and full descriptions for every tool on that server. Preferred when you know which server to use.
2. `{"server":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns the full schema and full description for one tool.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tool and server names across all servers using RE2 syntax (no backreferences, lookahead, or lookbehind). Use when you're unsure which server has the tool you need.
4. No arguments: returns a catalog of all servers with tool names and short descriptions. Only use this if you have no idea which server or tool to look for — in most cases, prefer fetching by server or pattern instead.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; server and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

MANDATORY - Always call `GetMcpTools` to discover a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallMcpTool`. If you already know the server, go directly to it rather than listing the full catalog first.

If the available MCP tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do with MCP and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing or unavailable MCP tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

Changelog
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

3.0.1 - 2026-07-06
Changed
Narrow Uint8Array type to ArrayBuffer only
Added Z_STREAM_ERROR check (reachable only via wrong options call)
3.0.0 - 2026-06-26
Added
Generated type definitions.
Low-level zlib API exports.
.onStart() hooks for advanced stream setup.
Changed
Switched sources to TypeScript, and tests, examples and benchmarks to ESM.
Changed exports to named-only. Use import * as pako from 'pako' instead of default import if you need the whole API as an object.
Changed package files layout. See package.json for supported entry points.
legacyHash default is now false. Binary output is now compatible with nodejs by default.
dictionary option now accepts only Uint8Array / ArrayBuffer (no String anymore).
.onEnd() now only assembles output chunks into result, and no longer sets the err / msg fields.
Use native TextEncoder / TextDecoder for string conversion. Removed shims.
Replaced { to: 'string' }) with { toText: true }) for UTF-8 text output in high-level helpers (inflate, inflateRaw, ungzip).
Build dist/ on publish instead of keeping generated bundles in git.
Inflate.push() after stream end returns the decode result, not always false.
Removed
Default export. import pako from 'pako' is no longer supported.
{ to: 'string' }) option from the streaming Inflate class. It now always emits byte chunks.
Automatic gzip header collection in Inflate. Use .onStart() with zlibInflateGetHeader() to read gzip metadata.
Prebuilt dist/ bundles from repository.
</user_query>

=== assistant ===
Yes — bumping alone doesn’t unlock the new surface. PPTist already uses OMML; the high-value unused pieces are where the **editor already has data** but export flattens or skips it.

### Highest payoff (editor already has it)
1. **Native gradients** — slide/shape gradients are mixed to a solid today; map to `fill: { type: 'linearGradient', stops, angle }`.
2. **Animations** — `slide.animations` is never read; map to `animation` / `appearOnClick` on text/shapes/images.
3. **Theme scheme** — `theme.themeColors` → `pptx.theme.themeColors` (12-slot) so accents/theme colors round-trip in PPT.
4. **`addFont`** — you only pass `fontFace` names; embed used webfonts/custom faces so machines without those fonts still render.

### Strong if you extend the model a bit
5. **Connectors** — lines are free custGeom; if you can attach line↔shape, use `isConnector` + `sId` + `pptx.anchor`.
6. **Richer bullets** — `bullet.color` / numbering (today only type + indent).
7. **Placeholder formatting** — master placeholders get geometry only; push font/size/color/align into master `placeholder` options.
8. **Image chrome** — `rectRadius`, outline, shadow (text boxes already get radius).

### Nice-to-have / chart-heavy
9. Table cell `vert` + real `vAlign` / strikethrough  
10. Chart `dataLabels` / `labelsRange` / `errorrate` / real series legends (only if the UI exposes them)

**Skip for now unless product asks:** compression enum, firstSlideNum, SVG `fill.color` recolor — smaller vs effort.

So: **no mandatory API rewrite for 4.1.3**, but the fork pays off if you wire gradients, animations, theme colors, and `addFont` first — those are the biggest fidelity gaps relative to what PPTist already stores.
